questions.question: Dr. Kamal must take an impression for a crown on a molar. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on physical properties, which material offers the best precision for a fixed prosthesis impression?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Addition silicones offer excellent dimensional stability and optimal precision for fixed prostheses.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use an addition silicone.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must take an impression for a study model. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on clinical properties, which impression material is most indicated for a study model?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Alginate is the material of choice for study models due to its low cost and ease of use.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use alginate for this study model.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal has taken an alginate impression and must pour it in plaster. Dr. Asma reminds him of the precautions. According to the principles of material vigilance, what is the major risk of alginate after its removal from the mouth?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Alginate is very sensitive to water variations; syneresis causes shrinkage, while imbibition causes expansion.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will pour the impression immediately.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must take an impression for an inlay. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on physical properties, which material offers the best reproduction of details for intracoronal preparations?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Polyethers offer excellent detail reproduction and ideal rigidity for intracoronal preparations.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a polyether.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must choose a plaster to make a working model for a crown. Dr. Asma asks him which type of plaster is most indicated. According to international standards, which plaster is used for high-precision working models?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Type IV plaster (high-strength stone) is used for high-precision working models in fixed prosthetics.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use Type IV plaster.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must make a study model for a removable prosthesis. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of plaster. According to mechanical properties, which type of plaster is indicated for study models?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Type II plaster is reserved for study and mounting models.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use Type II plaster for this study model.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must make a wax pattern for an inlay-core. Dr. Asma reminds him of the precautions. According to the physical properties of waxes, what is the major risk when handling a wax pattern?
options: Accumulation of internal stresses and relaxation over time
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Waxes accumulate internal stresses; prolonged storage can induce distortions.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will cast the pattern quickly.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must make a temporary crown on an incisor. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on aesthetic and mechanical properties, which material is most indicated?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Self-curing acrylic resins offer a good aesthetic and mechanical compromise for temporary crowns.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use an acrylic resin.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must cement a ceramic crown. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of cement. Based on adhesion properties, which cement offers the best bond to the ceramic?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Resin cements with silane offer excellent adhesion to ceramic after etching.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use a resin cement.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must cement a metal crown. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of cement. Based on clinical properties, which cement is most indicated for cementing metal crowns?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Glass ionomer cements offer good adhesion and fluoride release for metal crowns.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a GIC.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must take an impression for a 3-unit bridge. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on dimensional stability properties, which material is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Addition silicones offer optimal dimensional stability for bridge impressions.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use an addition silicone.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a temporary cementation on a temporary crown. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on clinical properties, which temporary cement is most indicated?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Zinc oxide-eugenol cement is ideal for temporary cementations due to its sedative properties.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use this temporary cement.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must choose a cement for definitive cementation on a ceramo-metal crown. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice. According to adhesion properties, which cement offers the best retention?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Resin cements offer the best retention for ceramo-metal crowns.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use a resin cement.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must make an occlusal registration. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on physical properties, which material is most indicated for an occlusal registration?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Bite registration silicones offer excellent precision for occlusal registrations.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use an occlusal silicone.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must take an impression for a complete removable prosthesis. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on clinical properties, which impression material is most indicated?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Alginate is the material of choice for primary impressions in complete removable prosthetics.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use alginate.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must choose a ceramic for an anterior single crown. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on aesthetic properties, which ceramic offers the best translucency?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Lithium disilicate offers excellent translucency for anterior crowns.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use lithium disilicate.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must make a zirconia infrastructure for a posterior bridge. Dr. Asma asks him about the advantages of zirconia. Based on mechanical properties, what is the major advantage of zirconia?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Zirconia offers exceptional flexural strength for posterior infrastructures.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use zirconia for this bridge.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must make a ceramic veneer. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on aesthetic properties, which ceramic is most indicated for veneers?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Lithium disilicate is the ceramic of choice for veneers due to its translucency and aesthetics.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use lithium disilicate.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must choose an alloy for a removable prosthesis framework. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice. According to mechanical properties, which alloy is most indicated for a removable prosthesis framework?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Cobalt-chromium offers exceptional rigidity and corrosion resistance for frameworks.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use cobalt-chromium.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must take an impression for an implant. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on physical properties, which material offers the best precision for implant-supported impressions?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Addition silicones offer optimal precision for implant-supported impressions.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use an addition silicone.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must choose a cement for definitive cementation on an implant. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice. According to clinical properties, which cement is most indicated for implant cementation?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Resin cements offer excellent retention for implant prostheses.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use a resin cement.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must make a temporary restoration on a prepared tooth. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on clinical properties, which material is most indicated for a long-term temporary restoration?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'High-performance polymers like PMMA offer excellent resistance for long-term temporaries.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use PMMA.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must take an impression for a ceramic inlay-onlay. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on physical properties, which material offers the best marginal precision?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Addition silicones offer exceptional marginal precision for inlays-onlays.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use an addition silicone.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must choose a material for a core build-up. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice. Based on mechanical properties, which material is most indicated?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'High filler content composites offer excellent resistance for core build-ups.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a high-strength composite.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal, after having performed several impressions and restorations with Dr. Asma, receives her congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Kamal?
options: Become an expert in materials and impression techniques
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Mastery of materials and impression techniques is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will train in new impression techniques.'
